subject: Coord: Dedicated capacity demo — slot orchestration & latency prep for Meridian Labs
messages:
From: Emma White <emma.white@meridianlabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput & latency overview

Hi Hannah,

I signed Meridian Labs up through the self-serve flow and we'd like to schedule a Dedicated capacity demo to validate throughput and latency under a production-like profile. High level: we run a retrieval + rerank + short generation pipeline (token lengths typically 64-512 tokens), current peak traffic is ~500 req/s, but we're planning a spike scenario targeting 2k concurrent sessions within a shard. Our p95 is usually ~60ms and p99 target for the end-to-end user-facing gen must stay under 200ms.

Key asks for the demo:
- Show Dedicated pool performance for steady and spike loads
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for 256/512 token paths
- How warm KV cache + batching affects tail latency

Availability (PST):
- Wed May 1: 09:00–12:00 or 15:30–17:00
- Thu May 2: 10:00–12:00

I can share a small sample traffic CSV and traces ahead of the call. Do you need any additional pre-read?

Thanks,
Emma White
Senior Engineering Manager, Meridian Labs
emma.white@meridianlabs.com
Attachments: sample_traffic.csv (CSV)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Emma White <emma.white@meridianlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput & latency overview

Hi Emma — thanks for the details and for signing up. Happy to coordinate a Dedicated demo focused on the points you called out. I looped in Ben (SE) so we can cover warm cache behavior and kernel/quantization trade-offs during the session.

Quick asks before we lock a slot:
- Can you confirm whether your traffic is bursty (short high-QPS bursts) vs. steady higher baseline?
- Typical prompt + response token sizes (examples are great)
- Any regulatory or VPC constraints we should be aware of for the demo environment

Proposed slots (PST):
- Wed May 1, 10:30 — 11:15 (30–45 min technical walkthrough)
- Thu May 2, 11:00 — 11:45 (preferred for SE availability)

I attached a one-page intake form to capture payload shapes; if you can fill that out before the call we'll tailor the runbook. HubSpot contact created: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/MB-789

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
SDR, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma White <emma.white@meridianlabs.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput & latency overview

Hi Emma — thanks for the context, Hannah. A few quick technical clarifications so we can prepare a meaningful Dedicated run: 
- Are the 500 req/s and 2k concurrent sessions counting inference tokens or higher-level requests (i.e., how many model retries, echo tokens)?
- Expected simultaneous sequence lengths for the spike case (avg/median/max)
- Are you using streaming or whole-response generation in your stack?

Depending on answers, we'll prepare two run profiles: 
A) steady high baseline with conservative batching, focusing on reserved pool sizing
B) bursty spike profile demonstrating autoscale/burst and graceful fallback to compatible variants

SE note: I have a calendar conflict on Wed May 1 at 10:30 PDT and won't be available then; Thu May 2 11:00 PDT works for me. If that slot is good for you we'll plan a 45-min technical session and a short canary run with prefix caching and synthetic load.

I've attached a short doc capturing the latency/throughput questions — it'll help speed the pre-call sync.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachments: latency_questions.docx (DOCX)
From: Emma White <emma.white@meridianlabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput & latency overview

Sounds good — Thu May 2, 11:00 PDT (11:00 — 11:45) works for us.

Answers to your quick clarifications:
- The 500 req/s is current steady peak at the router level; the 2k is a planned spike window counting top-level requests (we do not intentionally retry).
- Token sizes: typical prompts 40–120 tokens, responses 120–420 tokens; worst case ~512 tokens total.
- We use streaming in a subset of UIs but can run whole-response for the demo if that's easier.

I attached the sample traffic CSV and a small p99 trace bundle for your SE review. Please send a calendar invite or Zoom link and any pre-call checklist. Looking forward to the demo.
